# CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT

## 1. Identification of the Parties

This Agreement is made between It-product ("It-product", “Customer”)

with a principal place of business at 100 Main Street, New York, NY, United States, and NAME ("Consultant") with a principal place of business at ADDRESS.

title: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
section: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT > 2. Purpose of the Agreement
text:
## 2. Purpose of the Agreement

Customer desires to retain Consultant as an independent contractor to provide support for key Affordable Housing services (hereinafter "Services"). Consultant is willing and able to undertake the work and agrees to do so under the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement. Accordingly, the parties agree as follows.

title: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
section: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT > 3. Payment
text:
## 3. Payment

The agreed upon compensation is $xxxx USD (xxxx US dollars) per month.

Half of the invoice amount shall paid on the 15th of the month , and another half paid at the end each month. The invoices will be payable via PayPal, bank transfer/ACH or any other method as agreed upon by the parties.

title: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
section: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT > 4. Schedule and Location
text:
## 4. Schedule and Location

Consultant shall perform the tasks required of them remotely, from any location within Costa Rica, as long as performance of tasks at such location otherwise endangers or affects compliance with confidentiality obligations, as described below. Consultant shall dedicate specific number of hours per week to the Services and shall be available and reachable between hours of 7:00 AM Central Standard Time (“CST”) and 4:00 PM CST. The Customer will provide equipment , unless otherwise agreed.

title: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
section: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT > 5. Taxes and insurance
text:
## 5. Taxes and insurance

Consultant shall be solely responsible, to pay the corresponding taxes to the Costa Rican General Revenue Directorate (“Dirección General de Tributación”), and generally to comply with all applicable rules and regulations. Likewise, the Consultant shall register as taxpayer/contributor with the corresponding authorities, and as Independent Worker with CCSS (Caja Costarricense del Seguro Social).

title: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
section: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT > 5. Taxes and insurance
text: The Customer will have the right to demand proof of registration and insurance for tax and social security contributions, and failure to maintain registration and in good standing with either will be deemed as a material breach of this agreement allow Customer to rescind it.

title: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
section: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT > 6. Nature of relationship
text:
## 6. Nature of relationship

Both Consultant and Customer agree and acknowledge that the relationship hereby created is that of client and independent contractor. To that end, Consultant will be free to determine the manner of performance of the services that they are retained to provide, as long as it complies with the expected standards and levels of quality of the Customer.

title: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
section: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT > 6. Nature of relationship
text: Under no circumstance will the terms and conditions of this agreement, or the manner of performance between the parties, be interpreted to create or establish an employment relationship between the parties, nor will this agreement give rise to any labor or employment right or benefit for the Consultant.

title: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
section: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT > 7. Ownership of Intellectual Property
text:
## 7. Ownership of Intellectual Property

Consultant assigns to Customer its entire right, title and interest in anything created or developed by Consultant for Customer under this Agreement ("Work Product") including all patents, copyrights, trade secrets and other proprietary rights, including the rights to copy, sell, license, transfer, and otherwise commercialize the economic rights over the work.

title: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
section: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT > 7. Ownership of Intellectual Property
text: Consultant shall execute and aid in the preparation of any documents necessary to secure any copyright, patent, or other intellectual property rights in the Work Product at no charge to client. However, Customer shall reimburse Consultant for reasonable out-of-pocket expenses. (This provision survives for three years after expiration or termination of this Agreement.)

title: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
section: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT > 8. Confidentiality
text:
## 8. Confidentiality

1. All work completed in the performance of Services provided by Consultant shall be the property of It-product.

title: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
section: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT > 8. Confidentiality
text: 2. Consultant shall not, without It-product’s prior written permission, disclose any Confidential Information to any third party. “Confidential Information” shall include any information or material provided by or belonging to It-product that has not been made generally available to the public, whether or not expressed in a document or other medium and whether or not marked as confidential. Confidential Information or material may include, but is not limited to, past, present, and future inventions; past, present, and future communications between Consultant and It-product, or between Consultant and Project Manager; technical specifications, drawings, designs, prototypes, computer programs, databases, information, material, manufacturing activities, marketing plans, business plans, or sales strategy; that relate to or arise from information provided by It-product or Services provided by Consultant.

title: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
section: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT > 8. Confidentiality
text: 3. Consultant shall use Confidential Information only to provide Services to Customer and shall not use any Confidential Information for Consultant’s own business advantage or any other purpose without the prior written consent of Customer. Specifically, Consultant represents and warrants that he shall not derive any commercial benefit from the use of Confidential Information, other than the compensation for the Services provided to Customer under this Agreement.

title: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
section: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT > 8. Confidentiality
text:
4. Consultant represents and warrants that he shall not use Confidential Information for any purpose, which creates competition of any form for Customer, including but not limited to any competing venture controlled by Consultant and any third party.
5. title: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
section: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT > 8. Confidentiality
text:
6. Consultant further represents and warrants that he shall not incorporate into any prototype or other work product of Services performed, any copyrighted materials of any third party, unless authorized by Customer.
7. During the term of this Agreement and for three years afterward, Consultant will use reasonable care to prevent the unauthorized use or dissemination of Customer's confidential information. Reasonable care means at least the same degree of care Consultant uses to protect Consultant’s own confidential information from unauthorized disclosure. (This provision survives for three years after expiration or termination of this Agreement.)

title: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT

text:
## 9. Term of Agreement

This Agreement commences on HIRE DATE, and shall continue until full performance by both parties, until earlier terminated by one party under the terms of this Agreement, or until another Agreement modifies or substitutes this Agreement.

title: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT
section: CONSULTING AND CONFIDENTIAL SERVICES AGREEMENT > 10. Termination of Agreement
text:
## 10. Termination of Agreement

Each party shall have the right to terminate this Agreement by written notice to the other if a party has materially breached any obligation herein and such breach remains uncured for a period of 30 days after written notice of such breach is sent to the other party.

Each party shall have the right to terminate this Agreement for any reason upon 7 (seven) days' prior written notice to the other party. Upon such termination, all amounts owed to Consultant under this Agreement for accepted work shall immediately become due.

title: Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide
section: Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide
text:
# Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide

This guide is designed to support hiring Managers in forming interview questions. It is based on the Competency-Based Framework used by most international companies and includes tips for assessing both soft and hard skills. For additional support, please contact your HRBP, who can help develop questions or advise on behavioral interview techniques. 1.1 What is a Competency-Based Interview? These interviews assume that past behavior is the best predictor of future performance. Candidates are expected to provide real examples from their past experience.

title: Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide
section: Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide
text:
Competency-based (behavioral) questions evaluate how the candidateʼs personal qualities fit the role. Examples:
Tell us about a time you demonstrated leadership. Describe a difficult decision you had to make. Share a time when you showed initiative. Talk about how you overcame a major challenge. When did you refuse to compromise?

title: Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide
section: Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide
text:
1.2 Interview Format (Recommended balance):
50% — soft skills / competencies
40% — hard skills
10% — motivation
1.3 Competency-Based Interview Framework
This framework is aligned with company values and focuses on six key behavioral competencies. The STAR method helps assess candidate responses.

title: Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide
section: Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide
text:
STAR Method:
S – Situation: context of the experience
T – Task: what needed to be done
A – Action: what actions the candidate took
R – Result: what outcome was achieved
Tips for using STAR:
Ask for specific examples
Avoid vague questions like “How do you work in a team?”
Focus on actions, not generalizations
Compare answers to expected behavior for the role
Use answers for both internal and external feedback
Soft Skills (Competency) Assessment: One question per competency, evaluated using STAR.

title: Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide
section: Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide
text:
Hard Skills Assessment: Based on the job description, select 5–7 critical skills. Methods: STAR, practical tests, technical questions. Motivation Assessment: Understand reasons for job change and long-term engagement. 1.4 Competency Examples
1. Result Orientation
Describe a project with a tough deadline. How did you meet it? When did you exceed expectations? How? What do you do when a project risks falling behind? Have you ever taken on an “impossible” task? What helped? 2.

title: Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide
section: Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide
text:
Ownership
Have you taken on more responsibility than required? Share a failure. What did you do? Solved a problem independently? How? Ever improved a team process? What did you suggest? 3. Respect
Worked with someone very different? How did you get along? Faced conflict in a team? What was your role? Dealt with inappropriate behavior? What did you do? How do you give feedback without offending? 4. Teamwork
Describe your role in a team project. Helped the team resolve disagreements?

title: Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide
section: Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide
text:
What helps you sync with a new team? If a teammate struggles — whatʼs your action? 5. Changeability
Drastically changed plans mid-project? How did it go? Adapted to a changing project scope? Prefer predictable work or fast learning? Tackled a seemingly unrealistic task? How did you manage? 6. Continuous Improvement
How do you know when something needs improvement? Suggested a process improvement? What was it? Received tough criticism? How did you react? How do you stay updated in your field?

title: Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide
section: Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide
text: This guide is part of ʼs internal standards for recruitment and can be adapted for specific roles. The STAR method helps eliminate bias and structure evaluation clearly and fairly. It-product

title: Education Time Off
section: Education Time Off
text:
# Education Time Off

supports professional development that directly strengthens our work and teams. To that end, the following Education Time Off (ETO) guidelines apply:
Education Time Off Allowance
Each full time employee is eligible for 2 days per calendar year (16 hours) of paid Education Time Off. Part time employees are eligible for 8 hours per year. ETO does not roll over year to year and is not paid out if unused. Eligible Use
Education Time Off must be directly related to an employeeʼs current role. Employees must be able to demonstrate the expected benefit.

title: Education Time Off
section: Education Time Off
text:
The educational activity must clearly:
a. Enhance the employeeʼs current skill set, and
b. Provide meaningful knowledge or value to their team in the form of concrete documentation, industry contacts, or presentation style information sharing. Scheduling Requirements
Education Time Off must be requested at least one (1) month in advance of education start time. Education time can only be requested in 4 hour increments. Two days back to back will only be considered on a case by case basis. Approval Process
All ETO requests require committee approval.

title: Education Time Off
section: Education Time Off
text:
Employees should submit requests to their Director in the form of a google doc. Requests should include a brief explanation of the course or activity, with links and time commitments, along with an explanation of relevance to current work. Any fees associated should be outlined in full. Approved requests are then forwarded to Executive Leadership (CEO/COO/HR) for final approval. Requests will be evaluated within 5 business days
Approval is subject to business needs and staffing considerations. Questions should be directed to your Director or Executive Leadership. It-product

a. HR posts the vacancy on external job boards and platforms where has active accounts.
b. HR conducts an independent initial selection of relevant resumes.
c. HR shares shortlisted candidates with the Hiring Manager.
d. The Hiring Manager reviews the shortlist and provides timely feedback on which candidates should proceed further.

c. Upon the Managerʼs approval, HR schedules the first interview between the candidate and the Manager.
d. Standard interview duration: 30/60/90 minutes, depending on the role.

## 5. Feedback Collection and Assessment

a. The Hiring Manager provides structured feedback to HR within 2 working days after each interview.
b. If the candidate is not suitable, HR delivers a polite rejection.
c. If the candidate is suitable, HR sends the Predictive Index Behavioural Assessment.
d. Once completed, HR shares PI results with the Manager.
- PI is not a filtering criterion; it supports understanding of communication and work style.
e. If necessary, HR collects references at this stage.

Audience

- Employees — to take ownership of their professional development;
- Managers — to support and guide employee growth;
- HR — to facilitate and support the IDP process. Purpose
To provide a structured and scalable framework for setting individual development goals, fostering ownership, and supporting professional growth within / using Teamflect.

text:
## 1. IDP Ownership and System Usage

a. IDPs are created and maintained in Teamflect.
b. Access to Teamflect is available to all employees.
c. The Manager is responsible for:
- initiating the IDP in the system;
- ensuring the plan is created and updated;
- tracking progress.
d. The Employee is responsible for:
- actively participating in defining goals;
- completing planned development actions.
e. HR supports the process but does not own IDP creation.

text:
## 3. Creating an IDP in Teamflect

a. The Manager navigates in Teamflect:
- Career → Individual Development Plan
b. The Manager selects the relevant employee.
c. The Manager creates or updates the IDP, including:
- Career Objective
overall development direction
- Skills to Develop / Goals
2–3 key development areas
- Competencies to Work On
- Learning Materials or Courses Needed
d. Goals should be clearly defined and measurable (SMART approach recommended).
e. The IDP is saved and becomes visible to both Manager and Employee.

## 7. Specific Requirement: Affordable Housing Processing Team

a. For employees in the Affordable Housing Processing Team, salary reviews are conducted every 6 months.
b. The Hiring Manager is responsible for:
- tracking each employeeʼs 6-month review cycle;
- initiating salary review requests on time;
- ensuring no reviews are missed.
c. All reviews must be processed through BambooHR, following the standard process described above.

title: Values and Principles
section: Vision Statement
text:
#### Revised 9/18/2020

### Vision Statement

It-product’s overarching vision is to create the most reliable and respected property tax and affordable housing advisory firm in New York City. In the process, we nurture excellent and fulfilled employees and customers, invent new technologies and processes, and fuel the growth of It-product’s group of companies.

title: Values and Principles
section: Just Cause (updated 9/18/2020)
text:
### Just Cause (updated 9/18/2020)

We want to create a paradigm shift in how property owners relate to property management. We envision an environment where we can dramatically improve the data flow and understanding of property tax within the real estate industry, and eventually fix the system itself.

Why Statement (updated 9/26/2020):

We take responsibility for solving complex problems and creating efficiency so that our team and our clients can feel confident, empowered, and well taken care of.

In realizing our vision and moving toward our Why we use the following values and principles:

title: Values and Principles
section: Values and Principles > Expertise
text:
# Values and Principles

## Expertise

Our biggest asset is our people. We encourage our team to rapidly acquire and internalize the domain knowledge in every niche field of service. We strive to create and foster a productive learning environment, in which the practical application of rules and procedures is given a premium over simply studying the theory.

title: Values and Principles
section: Values and Principles > Expertise
text: We know the difference between experience and expertise. While most of our competitors may emphasize their decades of experience, they actually rely on an outmoded set of rules. Therefore, their so-called “experience” actually hinders real progress as they tend to stick to what they “know”. Knowing how things worked before is not enough to bring value in the 21st century.

title: Values and Principles
section: Values and Principles > Expertise
text:
Our starting point is to recognize that we do not know everything, but we will experiment and apply ourselves to find the best solutions and the most accurate answers. As true innovators of our industry, we actively seek additional knowledge and skills to respond to the changing regulatory landscape.

As a result, we develop unmatched expertise in all areas of service.

title: Values and Principles
section: Values and Principles > Innovation
text:
## Innovation

Innovation is what has defined our company since its inception. We think about process improvement every day. We invest heavily in technology and automation.

Not only do we innovate in making our clients experience better, but also by building time-saving and value-enhancing tools for our team internally. Unlike our competitors, who use pre-packaged technical and data solutions, we have developed our own client relationship management systems from scratch.

title: Values and Principles
section: Values and Principles > Innovation
text: Our innovation efforts permeate the business development efforts as we seek to serve our clients in new and better ways. For example, each year we experiment with adding at least one new service (revenue stream) to our existing line up of services. Sometimes, these new offerings do not scale and we have to quickly pivot away into different business lines. Sometimes, the new offerings turn into self-sufficient income-producing business units (e.g. Affordable Housing Unit).

title: Values and Principles
section: Values and Principles > Innovation
text: As a result of our focus on innovation our clients utilize the online portal, which allows for streamlined data collection and more efficient communication channels. We provide regular updates and reports filled with relevant actionable data. Our team is equipped with the best tools to perform their daily tasks, and our leadership seeks new opportunities to invest in technology.

title: Values and Principles
section: Values and Principles > Transparency
text:
## Transparency

We strive to offer our clients direct visibility into all of the processes relevant to their project. We accomplish this by regular status updates and customized reporting. Unlike many of our competitors, we do not obscure the full picture. Instead, we help our clients clearly understand the implications of our actions and their decisions.

title: Values and Principles
section: Values and Principles > Transparency
text:
For example, when a client is considering participation in a particular tax benefit program, we advise on all costs - including costs of compliance and opportunity costs - of both participating and not participating in the program. When a client wants to assess whether a certain filing is necessary, we go out of our way to explain all the cons and pros.

When the government agencies hide the facts out of convenience and other service providers obscure the truth for personal gains, we expose the data entirely for the benefit of our clients.

title: Values and Principles
section: Values and Principles > Breadth
text:
## Breadth

We pride ourselves in offering the full spectrum of relevant tax advisory services. Since there isn’t a single best way to optimize property taxes, we identify appropriate opportunities by tapping into our knowledge and expertise in multiple domains. We provide annual compliance and appeal services, file applications for project-based exemptions and abatements, help clients maintain the long-term tax benefits, offer tax projections and opinions, market and lease affordable units, among other relevant services. By offering a wide range of services, we can cover all of our clients’ needs.

title: Values and Principles
section: Values and Principles > Breadth
text: Our goal is to continually expand our service offerings by adding more value to our clients and more opportunities for our team’s professional development.

title: Values and Principles
section: Values and Principles > Fairness
text:
## Fairness

When it comes to tax assessment reductions, most taxpayers have been enduring a decades-long practice of being charged contingency fees they don’t fully understand. We reject the standard billing practice of charging a fee based on hypothetical future savings. Instead, our fee is based on the real tangible benefit that our clients realize an immediate result of our efforts.

In all other business units, we charge either flat fees or reasonable milestone-based fees upon delivery of certain agreed upon results.

title: Values and Principles
section: Values and Principles > Fairness
text: By not focusing on the short term self-benefit, we allow our customers to thrive and enjoy repeat business and referrals from most of them.

title: Values and Principles
section: Values and Principles > Client Amazement
text:
## Client Amazement

We design all of our communications and processes with the goal of amazing our clients. We strive to achieve excellence in the delivery of our services and in customer support. By nurturing relationships with our clients we establish the level of trust required for securing high value projects.

title: Values and Principles
section: Values and Principles > Client Amazement
text:
If we are unable to support a particular client, the principle of Client Amazement requires that we no longer do business together. Our commitment and efforts can only go so far. That is why we do not tolerate clients who exude pettiness, unjustified rudeness, unrealistic expectations, or tend to engage in unethical business practices.

When we align ourselves with the best companies in the real estate industry, our team feels empowered to deliver the best customer service.

title: Values and Principles
section: Values and Principles > The Long View
text:
## The Long View

The actions we take and the results we achieve do not occur in a vacuum.

We understand that the world of real estate has an enormous impact on the ecosystem of the City. Our careful approach to work ensures that we not only touch our clients in meaningful ways, but also have an indirect impact on the City and State agencies, the small businesses as well as families all throughout the City.

title: Values and Principles
section: Values and Principles > The Long View
text:
When faced with difficult challenges, we work closely on policy and procedure with the government agencies, encouraging them to implement recommended improvements. We are sensitive to our clients’ business relationships with their own stakeholders, and encourage them to take a long view in the decisions they make.

# Context

Our leasing team handles many apartment rental leases daily. We act as a third party between tenants and landlords during lease signing. We need a report showing leases that are in progress (not fully executed/signed yet) so we can track leases which are stuck at one stage for 3 days or more. There is a leasing platform, with which we send and sign leases.

title: Context

# Task

1. Suggest lease statuses. Draft a status workflow in any convenient way (simple table, diagram, etc).
2. Write a user story for the report + up to 5 acceptance criteria.

title: Context
section: Constraints
text:
# Constraints

- Keep it simple and practical (assume no deep domain knowledge).
- If you need to make assumptions, highlight them in your responses and list questions and you would ask to clarify with stakeholders.
- If there were lease statuses that you considered, but intentionally did NOT include, write a few words about it - what were they and why you decided not to include them.
- Try to work on the core of the tasks independently, without AI.

title: Rotation Between Departments/Roles
section: Rotation Between Departments/Roles
text:
# Rotation Between Departments/Roles

Rotation Eligibility Employees may be considered for a rotation to a different department or role based on business needs, growth opportunities, or organizational changes. Employees who wish to be considered for a rotation should first discuss this with their Manager and Human Resources. Raising the request does not guarantee a rotation; it remains subject to business needs and approval. Initiating a Rotation A rotation is initiated by the employee's Manager — either based on business needs or following a request raised by the employee.

title: Rotation Between Departments/Roles
section: Rotation Between Departments/Roles
text: If the rotation moves the employee to another Manager's team, the receiving Manager must approve the move before it proceeds. Once approved, the Manager notifies Human Resources and copies their own direct Manager on the notification. Terms and Approval The Manager(s) and Human Resources agree on the effective date, the new job title, department, and reporting manager, and whether a compensation change applies.

title: Rotation Between Departments/Roles
section: Rotation Between Departments/Roles
text: Human Resources reviews the employee's contract type (Gig Contract or employment agreement) to confirm whether a formal contract amendment is required and, for US employees, whether the new role affects the employee's exempt/non-exempt classification. Written Confirmation Human Resources issues a Rotation Confirmation Letter to the employee stating the new title, department, reporting manager, effective date, compensation (if changed), and the length of the adaptation period. The employee signs the confirmation before the effective date.

title: Rotation Between Departments/Roles
section: Rotation Between Departments/Roles
text:
System and Records Updates Once the rotation is confirmed:
Human Resources updates the employee's job title and reporting line in BambooHR. The Manager submits the compensation change request in BambooHR, if applicable. Human Resources submits a request through the to update the employee's title and department across all relevant work systems, effective the agreed date. Human Resources manually updates the employee's title in Timflect. Announcement Human Resources announces the rotation in the "New Hires and Changes" Teams channel.

title: Rotation Between Departments/Roles
section: Rotation Between Departments/Roles
text: Adaptation Period Employees who rotate into a new role go through an adaptation period of one (1) to three (3) months, with the exact length set by the Manager based on the seniority and complexity of the new role. During this period, the Manager(s) and Human Resources informally review how the employee is adjusting to the new role. Human Resources may schedule a check-in with the employee, if needed.

title: Rotation Between Departments/Roles
section: Rotation Between Departments/Roles
text:
If the rotation does not work out during the adaptation period, the Manager(s) and Human Resources may agree to return the employee to their previous role without initiating a formal performance management process. Completion At the end of the adaptation period, Human Resources records the outcome of the rotation in the employee's file, and the rotation is considered complete. Attachments:

### 1. Purpose and confidentiality

These guidelines define how HR and Accounting should handle individual requests for financial assistance or interest-free employee loans from employees physically located in Ukraine.
This is an internal reference for HR, Accounting, and authorized management. It is not a publicly announced employee benefit or an automatic entitlement. Requests are reviewed individually and require CEO approval.
HR and Accounting must treat all requests and supporting information as confidential and share them only with people involved in reviewing or processing the request.

### 2. Emergency Financial Assistance

2.1. Purpose
One-time, non-repayable financial assistance may be considered when an employee is directly affected by exceptional circumstances related to the war in Ukraine. 2.2. Eligibility and conditions
The employee must be physically located in Ukraine at the time of the request. The request must relate directly to the consequences of the war. The maximum amount is USD 500 per employee. Assistance may be granted no more than once per calendar year. The assistance is non-repayable. Each request is reviewed individually and is subject to CEO approval.

Damage to or loss of the employeeʼs home due to shelling or other war-related events. Forced relocation or evacuation due to military activity. Other exceptional and documented circumstances directly connected to the war. It-product It-outsource

The employee must be physically located in Ukraine at the time of the request. The employee should have at least six months of service. The employeeʼs direct manager should provide positive performance feedback, with no significant performance or conduct concerns. The loan is interest-free.

# Paid Holidays & Floating Holidays Policy

The Company observes designated U.S. holidays and provides additional Floating Holidays to allow employees in the EU Team to observe national public holidays.
Holiday benefits are available to eligible full-time employees.

title: Paid Holidays & Floating Holidays Policy
section: Paid Holidays & Floating Holidays Policy > Company Observed U.S. Paid Holidays (2026)
text:
## Company Observed U.S. Paid Holidays (2026)

The Company observes the following U.S. holidays:
New Yearʼs Day — January 1, 2026
Memorial Day — May 25, 2026
Independence Day — July 4, 2026
Labor Day — September 7, 2026
Thanksgiving Day — November 26, 2026
Christmas Day — December 25, 2026
If an employee is required or chooses to work on a Company-observed U.S. holiday, they may take an alternative paid day off, subject to manager approval.

title: Paid Holidays & Floating Holidays Policy
section: Paid Holidays & Floating Holidays Policy > Company Observed U.S. Paid Holidays (2026)
text:
If a Company-observed holiday falls on a weekend, the holiday will be observed on the nearest business day:
If the holiday falls on a Saturday, it will be observed on the preceding Friday. If the holiday falls on a Sunday, it will be observed on the following Monday. If a holiday falls within an approved vacation period, the employee will be paid for the holiday in addition to the vacation day.

title: Paid Holidays & Floating Holidays Policy
section: Paid Holidays & Floating Holidays Policy > Floating Holidays (EU Team)
text:
## Floating Holidays (EU Team)

In addition to Company-observed U.S. holidays, employees in the EU Team are entitled to five (5) Floating Holidays per calendar year. Floating Holidays are designated exclusively for observing official Ukrainian public holidays and may not be used as general-purpose paid time off, except as provided in the “Additional Use for Emergencies and Safety Situations” section below.

title: Paid Holidays & Floating Holidays Policy
section: Paid Holidays & Floating Holidays Policy > Floating Holidays (EU Team)
text:
For reference, Ukrainian public holidays in 2026 include:
New Yearʼs Day — January 1
International Womenʼs Day — March 8
Easter Sunday (Orthodox) — April 12
International Workersʼ Day — May 1
Victory Day over Nazism in World War II — May 8
Pentecost (Trinity) — May 31
Constitution Day of Ukraine — June 28
Statehood Day of Ukraine — July 15
Independence Day of Ukraine — August 24
Defender of Ukraine Day — October 1
Christmas Day — December 25
New Yearʼs Day (January 1) and Christmas Day (December 25) are observed as Companydesignated U.S. holidays and are not counted toward the EU Team Floating Holiday allowance, even though they are also official Ukrainian public holidays.

title: Paid Holidays & Floating Holidays Policy
section: Paid Holidays & Floating Holidays Policy > Floating Holidays (EU Team)
text:
Floating Holiday Conditions:
Employees may take no more than one (1) paid holiday day off within a 30-day period. A minimum of four (4) daysʼ notice is required. Requests must be submitted via BambooHR (Paid Days Off). Approval from the direct manager is required. Floating Holidays do not roll over to the next calendar year and are not paid out upon termination.

title: Paid Holidays & Floating Holidays Policy
section: Paid Holidays & Floating Holidays Policy > Additional Use for Emergencies and Safety Situations (Employees Based in Ukraine)
text:
## Additional Use for Emergencies and Safety Situations (Employees Based in Ukraine)

Due to the ongoing security risks in Ukraine, the Company provides additional flexibility in the use of Floating Holidays and time off for employees based in Ukraine. This flexibility is intended to address emergency situations or circumstances in which an employee reasonably feels unsafe due to war-related risks or other safety concerns. Under these exceptional circumstances, employees may request:
Floating Holidays (Paid Days Off)
Vacation Days
Unpaid Time Off
Such requests may be approved outside of standard scheduling requirements and may be submitted on short notice when necessary.

title: Paid Holidays & Floating Holidays Policy
section: Paid Holidays & Floating Holidays Policy > Additional Use for Emergencies and Safety Situations (Employees Based in Ukraine)
text: No detailed explanation is required when requesting time off for emergency or safety-related reasons. All requests must be submitted via BambooHR and approved by the direct manager. Managers are expected to review these requests promptly, taking into consideration employee safety and business continuity. This provision applies specifically to employees based in Ukraine and reflects the current operating environment.

title: Paid Vacation
section: Paid Vacation > Vacation Entitlement
text:
# Paid Vacation

## Vacation Entitlement

Employees are eligible for twenty-four (24) calendar days of paid annual leave in accordance with Ukrainian labor legislation.
Vacation accrues proportionally throughout the calendar year and is calculated daily based on the employee's continuous employment.
BambooHR is the Company's official system of record for vacation accrual and balances. The vacation balance displayed in BambooHR reflects the employee's earned (accrued) vacation entitlement.

title: Paid Vacation
section: Paid Vacation > New Hires
text:
## New Hires

Vacation begins accruing on the employee's hire date.
During the first six (6) months of continuous employment, employees may use only the vacation days that have been accrued and are displayed in the Time Off section of BambooHR.

title: Paid Vacation
section: Paid Vacation > Advance Vacation
text:
## Advance Vacation

After completing six (6) months of continuous employment, employees may request annual leave of up to twenty-four (24) calendar days.
Employees may also request vacation in excess of their accrued balance.
Advance vacation is considered on a case-by-case basis and requires approval from both the employee's direct manager and Human Resources.
If approved, the employee's vacation balance in BambooHR may become negative.
Future vacation accruals will automatically reduce any negative balance.

title: Paid Vacation
section: Paid Vacation > Year-End Process
text:
## Year-End Process

Unused earned vacation does not carry over to the following calendar year.
Any earned but unused vacation balance remaining as of December 31 will be paid through payroll.
Vacation accrual begins again on January 1 for the new calendar year in accordance with this policy.

title: Paid Vacation
section: Paid Vacation > Using Vacation
text:
## Using Vacation

Employees must obtain approval from their direct manager before taking vacation.
Once approved, employees must submit their vacation request through .
Vacation requests should be submitted at least two (2) weeks before the planned start date whenever reasonably possible.
Annual leave may be divided into multiple periods.
BambooHR
During martial law in Ukraine, employees may take vacation in increments of four (4) hours (0.5 working day).
Approval of vacation requests is subject to business needs.

title: Paid Vacation
section: Paid Vacation > Termination of Employment
text:
## Termination of Employment

Upon termination of employment:
Earned but unused vacation will be paid based on the accrued vacation balance recorded in BambooHR. Fractional balances are rounded using standard mathematical rounding (e.g., 5.49 = 5 days; 5.50 = 6 days).
If an employee has used more vacation than accrued, the corresponding amount will be deducted from the employee's final paycheck in accordance with applicable Ukrainian labor legislation.

## Attachment 5 – SMART Goals Guide & Explanation

SMART is a framework used to set clear, realistic, and measurable goals. Each goal in the PDP should follow this structure:

S – Specific: Clearly define what you want to achieve.
M – Measurable: Make sure the goal can be tracked and evaluated.
A – Achievable: Ensure the goal is realistic given the context.
R – Relevant: Align with your role and business priorities.
T – Time-bound: Set a deadline for completion.

Example SMART Goal 1: "Improve public speaking skills by preparing and leading one team presentation each month for 3 months, collecting peer feedback after each session."

Example SMART Goal 2: "Learn SQL basics by completing an online course and building 3 sample queries in production by September 30."

Tips:

- Break large objectives into small SMART sub-goals
- Avoid vague verbs like "improve" or "do more"—make it observable
- Use action words like build, write, lead, present, mentor

## Attachment 6 – What to Base the PDP On

PDPs can be grounded in various inputs depending on the context:

- Competency Matrix: Use if role expectations are formalized (good for Team Leads)
- Job Description: Use for performance ramp-up, onboarding, or promotions
- Behavioral Feedback: Best for correcting gaps (e.g., conflict avoidance, slow delivery)
- Employee Initiative: If someone wants to grow in a specific area (e.g., presentation skills)

Combine these for flexibility - e.g., JD + feedback + self-drive = strongest combo

# Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team

## Purpose

To define a consistent and transparent process for identifying, assessing, and hiring the right candidates across It-product. This ensures alignment with our company values, team needs, and operational structure.

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Process Overview
text:
## Process Overview

The recruitment process applies to all roles opened across It-product. It is coordinated by the HR Department in collaboration with the Hiring Manager (Team Lead or Department Head). The process includes five key phases:

1. Vacancy Initiation
2. Job Posting and Resume Selection
3. Prescreening and First Interview
4. Additional Stages (if needed)
5. Feedback Collection
6. Offer Preparation
7. Completion

Each phase involves clear responsibilities and shared decision-making to ensure both speed and quality.

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Process Overview > 1. Vacancy Initiation

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Process Overview > 2. Job Posting and Resume Selection
text:
### 2. Job Posting and Resume Selection

a. HR posts the vacancy on external sites where It-product has accounts:

- Work.ua, Djinni, DOU, HappyMonday, LinkedIn (access via Head of RO Oleg Marchenko)

b. If needed, vacancy payments are made by Head of RO Oleg Marchenko.

c. HR independently selects relevant resumes and shares them with the Manager.

d. The Manager chooses the most suitable candidates and provides feedback to HR.

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Process Overview > 3. Prescreening and First Interview
text:
### 3. Prescreening and First Interview

a. HR conducts an initial interview with candidates.

b. HR shares written feedback in Teams for candidates considered relevant.

c. Upon the Manager's approval, HR arranges the first interview between the candidate and the Manager.

d. Interview duration: 30/60/90 minutes (agreed individually).

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Process Overview > 4. Additional Stages (if needed)
text:
### 4. Additional Stages (if needed)

a. Additional technical interviews or meetings with other Managers may be held.

b. HR may or may not participate at this stage.

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Process Overview > 5. Feedback Collection
text:
### 5. Feedback Collection

a. The Manager provides feedback to HR via Teams or email (within 2 working days after the interview).

b. If the candidate is not suitable, HR sends a polite rejection.

c. If the candidate is suitable, HR sends a Predictive Index Behaviour Assessment for the candidate.

d. Once the candidate completes the test, HR shares the results with the Manager.

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Process Overview > 5. Feedback Collection
text:
- This test is not a key selection criterion, but it helps to better understand personality types, which is useful for internal rotations.
- Access to Predictive Index for HR is provided by the Head of RO Oleg Marchenko (login and password).

e. If necessary, HR collects references for the candidate at this stage.

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Process Overview > 6. Offer Preparation
text:
### 6. Offer Preparation

a. HR and the Manager align on the offer details: start date, salary, type of employment.

b. HR prepares and sends the offer letter to the candidate via email, CC the Head of RO and the Manager.

It is important to ensure the candidate submits all required personal documents before the offer is finalized. These documents must include:

section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Process Overview > 6. Offer Preparation
text:
- First and last name in English
- Copy of internal UA passport or ID card
- Tax ID (ІПН)
- Registration
- Residence address
- Phone number
- Email address
- Bank card number (only the number)

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Process Overview > 7. Completion
text:
### 7. Completion

a. After written confirmation from the candidate, the Head of RO or HR prepares the contract in Vchasno.

b. After the contract is signed, the Head of RO creates system accounts and sends login credentials to the candidate, with the Manager in CC.

c. The vacancy is considered closed. Next step: onboarding.

text:
## Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide

This guide is designed to support hiring Managers in forming interview questions. It is based on the Competency-Based Framework used by most international companies and includes tips for assessing both soft and hard skills.

For additional support, please contact your HRBP, who can help develop questions or advise on behavioral interview techniques.

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide > 1.1 What is a Competency-Based Interview?
text:
#### 1.1 What is a Competency-Based Interview?

These interviews assume that past behavior is the best predictor of future performance. Candidates are expected to provide real examples from their past experience.

Competency-based (behavioral) questions evaluate how the candidate’s personal qualities fit the role.

Examples:

- Tell us about a time you demonstrated leadership.
- Describe a difficult decision you had to make.
- Share a time when you showed initiative.
- Talk about how you overcame a major challenge.
- When did you refuse to compromise?

1.2 Interview Format (Recommended balance):

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide > 1.1 What is a Competency-Based Interview?
text:
- 50% — soft skills / competencies
- 40% — hard skills
- 10% — motivation

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide > 1.3 Competency-Based Interview Framework
text:
#### 1.3 Competency-Based Interview Framework

This framework is aligned with company values and focuses on six key behavioral competencies. The STAR method helps assess candidate responses.

STAR Method:

- S – Situation: context of the experience
- T – Task: what needed to be done
- A – Action: what actions the candidate took
- R – Result: what outcome was achieved

Tips for using STAR:

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide > 1.3 Competency-Based Interview Framework
text:
- Ask for specific examples
- Avoid vague questions like “How do you work in a team?”
- Focus on actions, not generalizations
- Compare answers to expected behavior for the role
- Use answers for both internal and external feedback

Soft Skills (Competency) Assessment: One question per competency, evaluated using STAR. Hard Skills Assessment: Based on the job description, select 5–7 critical skills. Methods: STAR, practical tests, technical questions.

Motivation Assessment: Understand reasons for job change and long-term engagement.

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide > 1. Result Orientation
text:
#### 1.4 Competency Examples

#### 1. Result Orientation

- Describe a project with a tough deadline. How did you meet it?
- When did you exceed expectations? How?
- What do you do when a project risks falling behind?
- Have you ever taken on an “impossible” task? What helped?

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide > 2. Ownership
text:
#### 2. Ownership

- Have you taken on more responsibility than required?
- Share a failure. What did you do?
- Solved a problem independently? How?
- Ever improved a team process? What did you suggest?

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide > 3. Respect
text:
#### 3. Respect

- Worked with someone very different? How did you get along?
- Faced conflict in a team? What was your role?
- Dealt with inappropriate behavior? What did you do?
- How do you give feedback without offending?

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide > 4. Teamwork
text:
#### 4. Teamwork

- Describe your role in a team project.
- Helped the team resolve disagreements?
- What helps you sync with a new team?
- If a teammate struggles — what’s your action?

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide > 5. Changeability
text:
#### 5. Changeability

- Drastically changed plans mid-project? How did it go?
- Adapted to a changing project scope?
- Prefer predictable work or fast learning?
- Tackled a seemingly unrealistic task? How did you manage?

title: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team
section: Recruitment Process. General Provisions for the EU Team > Attachment 2: Competency-Based Interview Guide > 6. Continuous Improvement
text:
#### 6. Continuous Improvement

- How do you know when something needs improvement?
- Suggested a process improvement? What was it?
- Received tough criticism? How did you react?
- How do you stay updated in your field?

This guide is part of It-product’s internal standards for recruitment and can be adapted for specific roles. The STAR method helps eliminate bias and structure evaluation clearly and fairly.

text:
# Commuter Benefits Policy

## (Effective May 1, 2026)

It-product provides a Commuter Benefit Program that allows employees to pay for eligible transportation expenses with pre-tax income. Employees are eligible to participate immediately upon hire. The program operates similarly to a Flexible Benefits Program, in which employees elect to have a portion of their pre-tax income allocated to an account for reimbursement of eligible transportation expenses.

Eligibility:

U.S.-based employees who are assigned to and commute to the New York office at least two days per week are eligible to participate in the Commuter Benefits Program.

title: Commuter Benefits Policy
section: Commuter Benefits Policy > (Effective May 1, 2026)
text: Employees who do not regularly commute to the office are not eligible for employer contributions but may be eligible to participate with employee-funded contributions, in accordance with plan rules.

title: Commuter Benefits Policy
section: Commuter Benefits Policy > Employer Contributions
text:
## Employer Contributions

It-product provides monthly commuter benefit contributions based on an employee’s in-office work schedule:

- Employees commuting 2–3 days per week: $75 per month
- Employees commuting 4–5 days per week: $132 per month

Employees participating in the program must elect to apply employer contributions to either transit benefits or parking benefits. Employer contributions will be added to employee accounts at the end of each month.

Employer contribution amounts are subject to applicable IRS limits, which may change annually.

title: Commuter Benefits Policy
section: Commuter Benefits Policy > Employee Contributions
text:
## Employee Contributions

In addition to the company contribution, employees may elect to contribute their own pre-tax income to their commuter benefits account, subject to IRS limits and plan guidelines.

Expertise

Our biggest asset is our people. We encourage our team to rapidly acquire and internalize the domain knowledge in every niche field of service. We strive to create and foster a productive learning environment, in which the practical application of rules and procedures is given a premium over simply studying the theory.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-1. Introduction 1-2. Vision Statement
text: We know the difference between experience and expertise. While most of our competitors may emphasize their decades of experience, they actually rely on an outmoded set of rules. Therefore, their so-called "experience" actually hinders real progress as they tend to stick to what they "know". Knowing how things worked before is not enough to bring value in the 21st century.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-1. Introduction 1-2. Vision Statement
text:
Our starting point is to recognize that we do not know everything, but we will experiment and apply ourselves to find the best solutions and the most accurate answers. As true innovators of our industry, we actively seek additional knowledge and skills to respond to the changing regulatory landscape.

As a result, we develop unmatched expertise in all areas of service.

Innovation

- Innovation is what has defined our company since its inception. We think about process improvement every day. We invest heavily in technology and automation.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-1. Introduction 1-2. Vision Statement
text: - Not only do we innovate in making our clients experience better, but also by building timesaving and value-enhancing tools for our team internally. Unlike our competitors, who use pre-packaged technical and data solutions, we have developed our own client relationship management systems from scratch.

- Our innovation efforts permeate the business development efforts as we seek to serve our clients in new and better ways. For example, each year we experiment with adding at least one new service (revenue stream) to our existing line up of services. Sometimes, these new offerings do not scale, and we have to quickly pivot away into different business lines.
Sometimes, the new offerings turn into self-sufficient income-producing business units (e.g., Affordable Housing Unit).

We provide regular updates and reports filled with relevant actionable data. Our team is equipped with the best tools to perform their daily tasks, and our leadership seeks new opportunities to invest in technology.

#### 1-3. Values and Principles
Transparency

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-1. Introduction 1-2. Vision Statement
text:
We strive to offer our clients direct visibility into all of the processes relevant to their project.
We accomplish this by regular status updates and customized reporting. Unlike many of our competitors, we do not obscure the full picture. Instead, we help our clients clearly understand the implications of our actions and their decisions.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-1. Introduction 1-2. Vision Statement
text:
For example, when a client is considering participation in a particular tax benefit program, we advise on all costs - including costs of compliance and opportunity costs - of both participating and not participating in the program. When a client wants to assess whether a certain filing is necessary, we go out of our way to explain all the cons and pros.

When the government agencies hide the facts out of convenience and other service providers obscure the truth for personal gains, we expose the data entirely for the benefit of our clients.

Breadth

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-1. Introduction 1-2. Vision Statement
text: We pride ourselves in offering the full spectrum of relevant tax advisory services. Since there isn't a single best way to optimize property taxes, we identify appropriate opportunities by tapping into our knowledge and expertise in multiple domains. We provide annual compliance and appeal services, file applications for project-based exemptions and abatements, help clients maintain the long-term tax benefits, offer tax projections and opinions, market and lease affordable units, among other relevant services. By offering a wide range of services, we can cover all of our clients' needs.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-1. Introduction 1-2. Vision Statement
text:
Our goal is to continually expand our service offerings by adding more value to our clients and more opportunities for our team's professional development.

Fairness

When it comes to tax assessment reductions, most taxpayers have been enduring a decadeslong practice of being charged contingency fees they don't fully understand. We reject the standard billing practice of charging a fee based on hypothetical future savings. Instead, our fee is based on the real tangible benefit that our clients realize an immediate result of our efforts.

In all other business units, we charge either flat fees or reasonable milestone-based fees upon delivery of certain agreed upon results.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-1. Introduction 1-2. Vision Statement
text:
By not focusing on the short-term self-benefit, we allow our customers to thrive and enjoy repeat business and referrals from most of them.

Client Amazement

We design all of our communications and processes with the goal of amazing our clients. We strive to achieve excellence in the delivery of our services and in customer support. By nurturing relationships with our clients, we establish the level of trust required for securing high value projects.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-1. Introduction 1-2. Vision Statement
text:
If we are unable to support a particular client, the principle of Client Amazement requires that we no longer do business together. Our commitment and efforts can only go so far. That is why we do not tolerate clients who exude pettiness, unjustified rudeness, unrealistic expectations, or tend to engage in unethical business practices.

When we align ourselves with the best companies in the real estate industry, our team feels empowered to deliver the best customer service.

The Long View

The actions we take and the results we achieve do not occur in a vacuum.

We understand that the world of real estate has an enormous impact on the ecosystem of the City.
Our careful approach to work ensures that we not only touch our clients in meaningful ways, but also have an indirect impact on the City and State agencies, the small businesses as well as families all throughout the City.

When faced with difficult challenges, we work closely on policy and procedure with the government agencies, encouraging them to implement recommended improvements. We are sensitive to our clients' business relationships with their own stakeholders and encourage them to take a long view in the decisions they make.

Harassment generally is defined in this policy as unwelcome verbal, visual or physical conduct that denigrates or shows hostility or aversion toward an individual because of any actual or perceived protected characteristic or has the purpose or effect of unreasonably interfering with an individual's work performance or creating an intimidating, hostile or offensive working environment.

Investigation Procedures
Upon receiving a complaint, the Company will promptly conduct a fair and thorough investigation into the facts and circumstances of any claim of a violation of this policy to ensure due process for all parties. To the extent possible, the Company will endeavor to keep the reporting individual's concerns confidential. However, complete confidentiality may not be possible in all circumstances. All individuals are required to cooperate in all investigations conducted pursuant to this policy. During the investigation, the Company generally will interview the complainant and the accused, conduct further interviews as necessary and review any relevant documents or other information.

title: Employee Handbook

text: Upon completion of the investigation, the Company will determine whether this policy has been violated based upon its reasonable evaluation of the information gathered during the investigation. The Company will inform the complainant and the accused of the results of the investigation. The Company will take corrective measures against any person who it finds to have engaged in conduct in violation of this policy, if the Company determines such measures are necessary. These measures may include, but are not limited to, counseling, suspension or immediate termination.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-1. Introduction 1-2. Vision Statement
text: The Human Rights Law (HRL), codified as N.Y. Executive Law, art. 15, § 290 et seq., applies to all employers in New York State with regard to sexual harassment, and protects employees, paid or unpaid interns and non- employees, regardless of immigration status. A complaint alleging violation of the HRL may be filed either with the Division of Human Rights (DHR) or in New York State Supreme Court.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-1. Introduction 1-2. Vision Statement
text: Complaints with DHR may be filed any time within three (3) years of the sexual harassment or within one (1) year of any other harassment. If an individual did not file at DHR, they can sue directly in state court under the HRL, within three (3) years of the alleged harassment. An individual may not file with DHR if they have already filed a HRL complaint in state court. Complaining internally to the Company does not extend the time to file with DHR or in court.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-1. Introduction 1-2. Vision Statement
text: An attorney is not needed to file a complaint with DHR, and there is no cost to file with DHR. DHR will investigate complaints and determine whether there is probable cause to believe that sexual harassment has occurred. Probable cause cases are forwarded to a public hearing before an administrative law judge. If sexual harassment is found after a hearing, DHR has the power to award relief, which varies but may include requiring the employer to take action to stop the harassment, or redress the damage caused, including paying of monetary damages, attorney's fees and civil fines.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-1. Introduction 1-2. Vision Statement
text: DHR's main office contact information is: NYS Division of Human Rights, One Fordham Plaza, Fourth Floor, Bronx, New York 10458; (718) 741-8400; www.dhr.ny.gov. Contact DHR at (888) 392-3644 or visit dhr.ny.gov/complaint for more information about filing a complaint. The website has a complaint form that can be downloaded, filled out, notarized and mailed to DHR. The website also contains contact information for DHR's regional offices across New York State.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-1. Introduction 1-2. Vision Statement
text:
Civil Rights Act of 1964
The United States Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) enforces federal antidiscrimination laws, including Title VII of the 1964 federal Civil Rights Act (codified as 42 U.S.C. § 2000e et seq.). An individual can file a complaint with the EEOC anytime within 300 days from the harassment. There is no cost to file a complaint with the EEOC.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-1. Introduction 1-2. Vision Statement
text: The EEOC will investigate the complaint and determine whether there is reasonable cause to believe that discrimination has occurred, at which point the EEOC will issue a Right to Sue letter permitting the individual to file a complaint in federal court. The EEOC does not hold hearings or award relief but may take other action including pursuing cases in federal court on behalf of complaining parties. Federal courts may award remedies if discrimination is found to have occurred. In general, private employers must have at least 15 employees to come within the jurisdiction of the EEOC.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-1. Introduction 1-2. Vision Statement
text: An individual alleging discrimination at work can file a "Charge of Discrimination." The EEOC has district, area and field offices where complaints can be filed. Contact the EEOC by calling 1-800-669- 4000 (TTY: 1-800-669-6820), visiting their website at www.eeoc.gov or via email at info@eeoc.gov. If an individual filed an administrative complaint with DHR, DHR will file the complaint with the EEOC to preserve the right to proceed in federal court.

title: Employee Handbook

text:
Local Protections
Many localities enforce laws protecting individuals from harassment and discrimination. An individual should contact the county, city, or town in which they live to find out if such a law exists. For example, those who work in New York City may file complaints of sexual harassment with the New York City Commission on Human Rights.

If the harassment involves unwanted physical touching, coerced physical confinement or coerced sex acts, the conduct may constitute a crime. Contact the local police department.

Employees have the right to request and use safe and sick time and may file a complaint for alleged violations of this policy with the New York City Department of Consumer and Workforce Protection or the New York State Department of Labor. provides paid prenatal personal leave to pregnant employees who work in New York State.

Grant

Eligible employees receive a grant of 20 hours of paid prenatal personal leave per 52-weeks.

Notice and Documentation

Employees must provide reasonable advance notice of the need to use paid prenatal personal leave to their manager.

Employees may carry over any unused sick and safe leave to the following calendar year.
However, employees only may use up to 40 hours in each calendar year. Unused safe and sick time will not be paid at separation.

#### 3-16. Commuter Benefit Program
If employees are called into active military service or enlist in the uniformed services, they will be eligible to receive an unpaid military leave of absence. To be eligible for military leave, employees must provide management with advance notice of service obligations unless they are prevented from providing such notice by military necessity or it is otherwise impossible or unreasonable to provide such notice. Provided the absence does not exceed applicable statutory limitations, employees will retain reemployment rights and accrue seniority and benefits in accordance with applicable federal and state laws.

Employees who have a regular work schedule of 20 or more hours per week and have been employed at least 26 consecutive weeks before the date Paid Family Leave (PFL) begins (or who have a regular work schedule of less than 20 hours per week and have worked at least 175 days to the date PFL begins) are eligible for PFL. Paid time off can be counted toward the employee's eligibility determination. Employees are eligible for PFL regardless of citizenship and/or immigration status.

text: PFL benefits are financed solely through employee contributions via payroll deductions. The weekly monetary benefit will be 67 percent of the employee's average weekly wage up to 67 percent of the state average weekly wage. The Company and the employee may agree to allow the employee to supplement PFL benefits up to their full salary with paid time off, to the maximum extent permitted by applicable law.

text: The employee who is eligible for both statutory short-term disability benefits and PFL during the same period of 52-consecutive-calendar weeks may not receive more than 26 total weeks of disability and PFL benefits during that period of time. Statutory short-term disability benefits and PFL benefits may not be used concurrently. If the employee is unable to work and qualifies for workers' compensation benefits, the employee may not use PFL benefits at the same time the employee is receiving workers' compensation benefits. The employee receiving reduced earnings may be eligible for PFL.

Definition of a Serious Health Condition
A serious health condition is an illness, injury, impairment or physical or mental condition that involves inpatient care in a hospital, hospice or residential health care facility, or continuing treatment or continuing supervision by a health care provider.

Use of Leave
The employee does not need to use this leave entitlement in one (1) block. Leave can be taken intermittently in daily increments. Leave taken on an intermittent basis will not result in a reduction of the total amount of leave to which the employee is entitled beyond the amount of leave actually taken.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 4 - Leaves Of Absence
text:
Employee Responsibilities
The employee must provide 30 days' advance notice before the date leave is to begin if the qualifying event is foreseeable. When 30 days' notice is not practicable for reasons such as a lack of knowledge of approximately when leave will be required to begin, a change in circumstances, or a medical emergency, the employee must provide notice as soon as practicable and generally must comply with the Company's normal call-in procedures.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 4 - Leaves Of Absence
text: Failure by the employee to give 30 days' advance notice of a foreseeable event may result in partial denial of the employee's benefits for a period of up to 30 days from the date notice is provided. Employees must provide sufficient information to make the Company aware of the qualifying event and the anticipated timing and duration of the leave. Employees must specifically identify the type of family leave requested. Employees also must provide medical certifications and periodic recertification or other supporting documentation or certifications supporting the need for leave.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 4 - Leaves Of Absence
text: The employee requesting PFL must submit a completed Request for Paid Family Leave or PFL-1 form and additional certification form(s) as follows to the Company's insurance carrier: 1) Bonding Certification: PFL-2 Form plus documentation; 2) Health Care Provider Certification: PFL-4 Form plus Personal Health Information (PHI) Release (PFL-3 Form); or 3) Military Qualifying Event: PFL-5 Form plus documentation. These documents are available from the Head of Human Resources. The Company's insurance carrier is NYSIF.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 4 - Leaves Of Absence
text: To submit a request for PFL, employees must complete the employee's portion of the insurance carrier's PFL-1 Form and submit it to Human Resources. The Company will complete its section of the form and will return it to the employee within three (3) business days. If the Company fails to respond, employees may submit all materials directly to the insurance carrier. Depending on the type of PFL leave employees are seeking, employees will be required to complete additional PFL forms as described in the communication that employees will receive from the insurance carrier.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 4 - Leaves Of Absence
text: Employees must submit the completed PFL forms before or within 30 days after the start of their leave. The insurance carrier must pay or deny leave requests within 18 calendar days of receiving the employee's completed forms.

title: Employee Handbook

text:
Job Benefits and Protection
During any PFL taken pursuant to this policy, the Company will maintain coverage under any existing group health insurance benefits plan as if the employee had continued to work. The employee must make arrangements with CEO and Head of Human Resources prior to taking leave to pay their portion of any applicable health insurance premiums each month. The Company's obligation to maintain health insurance coverage ceases if the employee's premium payment is more than 30 days late.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 4 - Leaves Of Absence
text: If the employee's payment is more than 15 days late, the Company will send a letter notifying the employee that coverage will be dropped on a specified date unless the co-payment is received before that date. Employees who exercise their right to PFL will, upon the expiration of that leave, be entitled to be restored to the position they held when the leave commenced, or to a comparable position with comparable benefits, pay and other terms and conditions of employment. The taking of leave covered by PFL will not result in the loss of any employment benefit accrued before the date on which the leave commenced.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 4 - Leaves Of Absence
text: While on PFL, employees will not continue to accrue sick or vacation time.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 4 - Leaves Of Absence
text:
Questions and/or Complaints About PFL
If employees have any questions regarding this policy, they should contact the Head of Human Resources. For additional information concerning leave entitlements and obligations that might arise when PFL is either not available or exhausted, employees should consult the Company's other leave policies or contact Human Resources. The Company is committed to complying with the PFL and will interpret and apply this policy in a manner consistent with the PFL. Employees who disagree with a denial of their claim for PFL may submit their dispute to arbitration. Employees will be provided with information about how to request arbitration.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 4 - Leaves Of Absence
text: Employees are protected from discrimination and retaliation for requesting or taking PFL. If employees believe their rights have been violated and/or they have been denied job restoration as a result of requesting and/or taking PFL, they must send the Head of Human Resources a formal request for job reinstatement using the Formal Request for Reinstatement Regarding Paid Family Leave (Form PFL-DC- 119), which can be found in the forms section of https://www.ny.gov/PaidFamilyLeave. Employees must file the completed form with the Company and send a copy to: Paid Family Leave, P.O.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Table of Contents > Section 4 - Leaves Of Absence
text: Box 9030, Endicott, NY 13761-9030. If the Company does not comply with the employee's request for reinstatement within 30 days, the employee may file a PFL discrimination complaint with the Workers ‘Compensation Board using the Paid Family Leave Discrimination Complaint (Form PFL -DC-120), which is also available on the New York PFL website. Once the employee's complaint is received, the Board will assemble the employee's case and schedule a preliminary hearing in front of a workers' compensation law judge.

Obviously, not every type of misconduct can be listed. Note that all employees are employed at-will, and reserves the right to impose whatever discipline it chooses, or none at all, in a particular instance. The Company will deal with each situation individually and nothing in this handbook should be construed as a promise of specific treatment in a given situation. However, will endeavor to utilize progressive discipline but reserves the right in its sole discretion to terminate the employee at any time for any reason.
The observance of these rules will help to ensure that our workplace remains a safe and desirable place to work.

title: Employee Handbook
