text: Employees are hired to perform important functions at . As with any group effort, operating effectively takes cooperation and commitment from everyone. Therefore, attendance and punctuality are very important. Unnecessary absences and lateness are expensive, disruptive and place an unfair burden on fellow employees and Supervisors. We expect excellent attendance from all employees. Excessive absenteeism or tardiness will result in disciplinary action up to and including discharge. We do recognize, however, there are times when absences and tardiness cannot be avoided.

The purpose of this plan is to protect employees against exposure and disease during an airborne infectious disease outbreak. This plan goes into effect when an airborne infectious disease is designated by the New York State Commissioner of Health as a highly contagious communicable disease that presents a serious risk of harm to the public health. This plan is subject to amendments and changes, which will be communicated to the employees before they take effect.

Employees should report any questions or concerns with the implementation of this plan to the Chief Operations Officer.

MINIMUM CONTROLS DURING AN OUTBREAK
During an airborne infectious disease outbreak, the following minimum controls will be used in all areas of the worksite:

1. General Awareness
Individuals may not be aware that they have the infectious disease and can spread it to others. Employees should remember to:

- Maintain physical distancing, if possible.

- Wear face coverings when social distancing is not possible.

- Wash hands properly and often or use hand sanitizer.

Hand Hygiene
To prevent the spread of infection, employees should wash hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds or use a hand sanitizer with at least 60% alcohol to clean hands BEFORE and AFTER:
- Touching your eyes, nose, or mouth.
- Touching your mask.
- Entering and leaving a public place; and
- Touching an item or surface that may be frequently touched by other people, such as door handles, tables, gas pumps, shopping carts, or electronic cashier registers/screens.
- Because hand sanitizers are less effective on soiled hands, wash hands rather than using hand sanitizer when your hands are soiled.

Because infectious diseases can be spread by droplets expelled from the mouth and nose, employees should exercise appropriate respiratory etiquette by covering nose and mouth when sneezing, coughing or yawning.

ADVANCED CONTROLS DURING AN OUTBREAK
For activities where the Minimum Controls alone will not provide sufficient protection for employees, additional controls may be necessary, such as improved ventilation. Advanced administrative controls may include the following:
- Increasing the space between workers.
- Employee training.
- Identify and prioritize job functions that are essential for continuous operations.
- Cross-train employees to ensure critical operations can continue during worker absence.
- Rearrange traffic flow to allow for one-way walking paths.
- Provide clearly designated entrance and exits.

#### 1-1. Introduction

text:
#### 1-2. It-product Vision Statement

It-product's overarching vision is to create the most reliable and respected property tax and affordable housing advisory firm in New York City. In the process, we nurture excellent and fulfilled employees and customers, invent new technologies and processes, and fuel the growth of It-product's group of companies.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Employee Handbook > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-2. It-product Vision Statement > Just Cause
text:
###### Just Cause

We want to create a paradigm shift in how property owners relate to property management.

Property Tax Arena:

We envision an environment where we can dramatically improve the data flow and understanding of property tax within the real estate industry, and eventually fix the system itself.

Affordable Housing Arena:

We want to reduce transaction costs, remove complexities and inequities in the process of supplying the affordable housing to NYC residents and beyond.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Employee Handbook > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-2. It-product Vision Statement > Why?
text:
###### Why?

We are passionate about taking responsibility for solving complex problems and creating efficiency so that our team and our clients can feel confident, empowered, and well taken care of.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Employee Handbook > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-3. Values and Principles > Expertise
text:
#### 1-3. Values and Principles

###### Expertise

Our biggest asset is our people. We encourage our team to rapidly acquire and internalize the domain knowledge in every niche field of service. We strive to create and foster a productive learning environment, in which the practical application of rules and procedures is given a premium over simply studying the theory.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Employee Handbook > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-3. Values and Principles > Expertise
text: We know the difference between experience and expertise. While most of our competitors may emphasize their decades of experience, they actually rely on an outmoded set of rules. Therefore, their so-called "experience" actually hinders real progress as they tend to stick to what they "know". Knowing how things worked before is not enough to bring value in the 21st century.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Employee Handbook > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-3. Values and Principles > Expertise
text:
Our starting point is to recognize that we do not know everything, but we will experiment and apply ourselves to find the best solutions and the most accurate answers. As true innovators of our industry, we actively seek additional knowledge and skills to respond to the changing regulatory landscape.

As a result, we develop unmatched expertise in all areas of service.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Employee Handbook > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-3. Values and Principles > Innovation
text:
###### Innovation

- Innovation is what has defined our company since its inception. We think about process improvement every day. We invest heavily in technology and automation.
- Not only do we innovate in making our clients experience better, but also by building time- saving and value-enhancing tools for our team internally. Unlike our competitors, who use pre-packaged technical and data solutions, we have developed our own client relationship management systems from scratch.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Employee Handbook > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-3. Values and Principles > Innovation
text: - Our innovation efforts permeate the business development efforts as we seek to serve our clients in new and better ways. For example, each year we experiment with adding at least one new service (revenue stream) to our existing line up of services. Sometimes, these new offerings do not scale, and we have to quickly pivot away into different business lines. Sometimes, the new offerings turn into self-sufficient income-producing business units (e.g., Affordable Housing Unit).

title: Employee Handbook
section: Employee Handbook > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-3. Values and Principles > Innovation
text: - As a result of our focus on innovation our clients utilize the online portal, which allows for streamlined data collection and more efficient communication channels. We provide regular updates and reports filled with relevant actionable data. Our team is equipped with the best tools to perform their daily tasks, and our leadership seeks new opportunities to invest in technology.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Employee Handbook > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-3. Values and Principles > Transparency
text:
###### Transparency

We strive to offer our clients direct visibility into all of the processes relevant to their project. We accomplish this by regular status updates and customized reporting. Unlike many of our competitors, we do not obscure the full picture. Instead, we help our clients clearly understand the implications of our actions and their decisions.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Employee Handbook > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-3. Values and Principles > Transparency
text:
For example, when a client is considering participation in a particular tax benefit program, we advise on all costs - including costs of compliance and opportunity costs - of both participating and not participating in the program. When a client wants to assess whether a certain filing is necessary, we go out of our way to explain all the cons and pros.

When the government agencies hide the facts out of convenience and other service providers obscure the truth for personal gains, we expose the data entirely for the benefit of our clients.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Employee Handbook > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-3. Values and Principles > Breadth
text:
###### Breadth

We pride ourselves in offering the full spectrum of relevant tax advisory services. Since there isn't a single best way to optimize property taxes, we identify appropriate opportunities by tapping into our knowledge and expertise in multiple domains. We provide annual compliance and appeal services, file applications for project-based exemptions and abatements, help clients maintain the long-term tax benefits, offer tax projections and opinions, market and lease affordable units, among other relevant services. By offering a wide range of services, we can cover all of our clients' needs.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Employee Handbook > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-3. Values and Principles > Breadth
text: Our goal is to continually expand our service offerings by adding more value to our clients and more opportunities for our team's professional development.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Employee Handbook > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-3. Values and Principles > Fairness
text:
###### Fairness

When it comes to tax assessment reductions, most taxpayers have been enduring a decades- long practice of being charged contingency fees they don't fully understand. We reject the standard billing practice of charging a fee based on hypothetical future savings. Instead, our fee is based on the real tangible benefit that our clients realize an immediate result of our efforts.

In all other business units, we charge either flat fees or reasonable milestone-based fees upon delivery of certain agreed upon results.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Employee Handbook > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-3. Values and Principles > Fairness
text: By not focusing on the short-term self-benefit, we allow our customers to thrive and enjoy repeat business and referrals from most of them.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Employee Handbook > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-3. Values and Principles > Client Amazement
text:
###### Client Amazement

We design all of our communications and processes with the goal of amazing our clients. We strive to achieve excellence in the delivery of our services and in customer support. By nurturing relationships with our clients, we establish the level of trust required for securing high value

projects.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Employee Handbook > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-3. Values and Principles > Client Amazement
text:
If we are unable to support a particular client, the principle of Client Amazement requires that we no longer do business together. Our commitment and efforts can only go so far. That is why we do not tolerate clients who exude pettiness, unjustified rudeness, unrealistic expectations, or tend to engage in unethical business practices.

When we align ourselves with the best companies in the real estate industry, our team feels empowered to deliver the best customer service.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Employee Handbook > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-3. Values and Principles > The Long View
text:
###### The Long View

The actions we take and the results we achieve do not occur in a vacuum.

We understand that the world of real estate has an enormous impact on the ecosystem of the City. Our careful approach to work ensures that we not only touch our clients in meaningful ways, but also have an indirect impact on the City and State agencies, the small businesses as well as families all throughout the City.

title: Employee Handbook
section: Employee Handbook > Section 1 - Governing Principles Of Employment > 1-3. Values and Principles > The Long View
text: When faced with difficult challenges, we work closely on policy and procedure with the government agencies, encouraging them to implement recommended improvements. We are sensitive to our clients' business relationships with their own stakeholders and encourage them to take a long view in the decisions they make.
